title: Handle invalid forms
body:
Send user feedback if an incomplete form is sent.

Some possible responses:
- if form is not in the db: send them a message that an invalid form was submitted.
- if the form is in the db but data not complete: send them a message asking them to complete the data and resend.

title: add required fields to smsforms
body:
Right now we don't have a notion of required fields or not in sms forms.  We need to include the option of required fields in textforms (higher priority) and muvuku forms. 

For example this form by default should require all fields:

```
exports['CNPW'] = {
    fields: [
        {key: 'wkn', label: 'Week number', type: 'number'},
        {key: 'wks', label: 'Number of weeks', type: 'number'},
        {key: 'afp', label: 'Acute Flaccid Paralysis', type: 'number'},
        {key: 'nnt', label: 'Neonatal Tetanus', type: 'number'},
        {key: 'msl', label: 'Measles', type: 'number'},
        {key: 'aes', label: 'Acute Encephalitis Syndrome', type: 'number'}
    ],
    data_record_type: "cdc_nepal"
};
```

If you want a field not required then we include `required: false` as an attribute.  Like `{key: 'afp', label: 'Acute Flaccid Paralysis', type: 'number', required: false}`.

Additionally a message should be generated when a form is submitted that does not validate, i.e. required attributes are not respected. Similar to what you've done in #46 except applies to all forms.

title: spreadsheet -- add validation to phone numbers column
body: Right now we are matching on this `/.*(\+\d{11}).*/` regex for validation of phone numbers in other areas of the app.  We might want to add this type of validation support to the spreadsheet.  This would likely include some hinting or way to communicate to the user they need to comply with a specific format.  The phone number formats in the spreadsheet and the sms message coming from the gateway, which is already formatted like the above regex, needs to match.  A problem can occur if the user enters a phone number that does not exactly match the string then the facility relation will fail to get attached to the record.  The regex support/validation in the spreadsheet seems like a quick solution and can be reused for other cells also.  For now it doesn't need to be that fancy, we can optimize it as we go and see how people interact with it.  I'm not sure where we are with validating cells in the spreadsheet but that would probably be the main goal of this ticket.

title: add form validation to sentinel
body: we should be able to validate a form within sentinel, this means porting the `packages/kujua-sms` library to sentinel, and thinking about what to leave in the couchapp.  Has potential to break forms, would involve migrating all forms to be processed by sentinel. title: [Requirement] Hook infrastucture to run functions on incoming message
body:
Many projects need to take custom action on incoming messages, such as forwarding based on a criteria/calculation, or registration for a notification schedule. Modularizing these functions so that they can be dropped into then read from a particular folder would make it easier for partner's developers or our team to write, test and deploy.

Ideally these function would access a Kujua API, but in the meantime CouchDB would be necessary.

[Requirement] UX improvement to User Management
body:
The functional issues from the last acceptance testing were listed in #344, but we could see that user management needs some UX improvements as well.

The staff that will create/update users have a wide range of IT skills so they need a more streamlined way to manage users. Currently all the user management is done as generic user management in Dashboard, as a parallel to the Facilities management in Kujua. In the long run this will be re-factored into a single Kujua Module, as was originally planned for v1.

Until then, there are some ways that we can make the user creation process simpler which will bring us a step closer to the refactor as well:
- Admin to change/rest a user's password in Dashboard garden20/dashboard#57
- Basic user management in Kujua itself for admin. Start with a "create new user" modal with the following fields: _username_, _user type_, _facility_, _locale_, _phone number_. [More details here](https://docs.google.com/a/medicmobile.org/drawings/d/1jHIRwwtkyw0voUHlFOvNtFIBbGfxyNh4ZScv3winZPA/edit)

Please add further suggestions on this thread.

currently the "search" and "filters" work separately.  So you can search by field names like `year:2013 AND month:2` but you can't filter by a facility and combine that with a the search fields.  

Change the filters to work using couchdb-lucene then we can combine all these different searches variables.  We can also remove the extra views/indexes that were needed to support the filters.  Also make sure to maintain/enforce facility based authorization on these filters, by checking user affiliation.

title: limit outgoing message queue
body: In some cases if the gateway is left off for a long period, many messages will get queued up.  This can cause problems on the gateway since there is a limit to how much data it can process.  Limit these to 25 messages for time being.  So if 500 messages are on the outbound queue then it will take 20 minutes to clear that queue if the gateway is set to poll every minute.  We can increase this limit later if we notice a problem, or make it a setting.

New setting to allow district administrators to see messages from unassigned contacts
body:
Currently messages and reports received from numbers that are not assigned to a facility are only viewable by national admin users. That means that only national admins can deal with these messages and assign them to facilities. If there are a lot of unassigned messages/reports then the burden for going through these can be quite high. For some deployments (but not all) it makes sense for the district manager to be able to see these messages as well. We could create an option in the settings for these messages to be seen by district admins as well. The default should remain that only national admins can see unassigned messages.

More succinctly: 
"As a national admin I want let district admins see unassigned messages and reports so that the burden of going through these messages doesn't fall entirely on me."

[requested by @ranjuts]

title: Filter the message export
body:
We need a mechanism to obtain subsets of the data when exporting messages so that we can process the resulting CSV files with our automated Analytics tools.

For some current projects the message export is yielding csv files that are too large to be processed by Analytics (10 MB limit), and our Middleware Google Scripts (30 sec timeout while processing).

We can currently filter messages by specifying url params for start and end date, which filter based on the `Reported Date`. This works to reduce the size, but the CSV output does not contain what a user would expect. Scheduled messages always have a `Reported Date` based on the report that generated them, regardless of when the scheduled message actually goes out. For example, filtering for messages in March will yield those _scheduled in March_, even if they are only going to be _sent in July_. Conversely, it will omit many of the messages actually sent in March since they are likely associated to a reported date from a previous month.

Eventually we would want a flexible mechanism to fully query the data. Given that this may be a large refactor that will rely heavily on Lucene, in the meantime it would be a huge benefit for projects that are in a standstill if they are able to filter a single individual column.

For instance, using the scheduled message example from above, using a url param to filter on column `Sent Timestamp` for messages in March (using appropriate timestamps), we would get a CSV that includes only messages that were actually sent in March. 

Although the main priority is having the range filters on any of the time fields, if it is possible at this time it would be nice to also include filtering any row based on sets of values. For instance, to only export the incoming messages, you could specify a filter on column `Message Type` to be `Incoming Message`. Another nice to have would be combining multiple filters e.g. a timestamp filter on `Scheduled Timestamp` with a particular schedule name as `Message Type` which is sent to a specific `To Phone`. I suspect that this is pushing the limit giving our current framework, just wanted to put that out there in case it can be done reasonably prior to the move to a more flexible querying system.

title: Grouped messages can be separated if registration has an offset
body:
This is a tricky situation because there is no official appointment or key in a group; all messages in a group are currently treated equal. However, _as a CHW I dont want to get followup messages of appointments notifications that would have occured prior to registration._ 

Normally this is not a problem because schedules start from the registration time. For registrations that have a date offset, such as LMP or DOB, it is possible that the registration is between messages of a group.

For example, in this config, there is a one week gap between messages in a group. The first is to remind a patient to go to the clinic, the second is a followup message to see if the patient attended the appointment:

```
    "schedules": [
        {
            "name": "ANC Reminders LMP",
            "start_from": "lmp_date",
            "messages": [
                {
                    "message": [
                        {
                            "content": "Please remind {{patient_name}} ({{patient_id}}) to visit health facility for ANC visit this week. When she does let us know with 'V {{patient_id}}'. Thanks!",
                            "locale": "en"
                        }
                    ],
                    "group": 1,
                    "offset": "12 weeks",
                    "send_day": "monday",
                    "send_time": "09:00",
                    "recipient": "reporting_unit"
                },
                {
                    "message": [
                        {
                            "content": "Did {{patient_name}} attend her ANC visit? When she does, respond with 'V {{patient_id}}'. Thank you!",
                            "locale": "en"
                        }
                    ],
                    "group": 1,
                    "offset": "13 weeks",
                    "send_day": "monday",
                    "send_time": "10:00",
                    "recipient": "reporting_unit"
                }
```

The result is that you get a followup about an appointment that would have occured prior to the registration:
![schedule messages regardless of group](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/3294853/d95438b2-f5b1-11e3-89b3-a8beca2ee058.png)

title: Summary of label updates for Reports tab
body:
Overall the report page is looking great! Now that we have had some use with data in a realistic scenario, here are some notes to improve the usability:
1. Message --> Automated Reply
2. Scheduled Tasks --> Scheduled Messages
3. In the facility label Include delimiter (eg ») between levels of the hierarchy
4. If facility is found, the name is more important than the number. In right pane make the facility label more prominent than the number, but keep the number. The left pane is a little trickier due to space constraints, but I would remove the number altogether for the known facilities.
5. Use the default datetime in the right pane, otherwise no clear way to know exactly when a message was sent, keep relative date in left pane.
6. Message and Task's times should be absolute datetime, not relative. Otherwise it is hard to differentiate when messages will actually go out, especially when they are within weeks of each other as it is for appointments. We should try to include the time too if possible because it helps a worker know when a message goes out. The hover over can be the relative date.

body:
The way we do settings has changed since #397, as evidenced in #596, and it is not entirely clear who we let actually access the configuration settings. Taking these changes into account it seems as though the pages that need couchdb admin credentials (Settings, Schedules, and Users because they either save in `app_settings` or create new couch users) are only accessible to true couchdb admins (which cannot be created from the User page*).

body:
Here are some UI updates from our designer Lester, my notes in parentheses or where marked.
1. **Swap tab colours:**

**Messages** - blue (instead of teal)
**Reports** - yellow (instead of orange... not sure if "yellow" is the current orange, so use orange for now until we get color value from Lester)
**Analytics** - teal (instead of blue)

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/4150411/76397a42-343d-11e4-9822-88362b50befa.png)

**Left panel:**
2. The “active” highlight color should be a tint of the color tab. eg light blue for Messages
3. More distinction for unread conversations/reports. (Lester suggested a blue dot but I dont want to confuse that with the valid/invalid in reports. Lets take a page from gmail:
**unread:** white background and bold text
**read:** light grey background `rgb ( 240, 240, 240 )`, unbolded
**hover:** indicator on left side of box, or "glow" around the message. This wont really apply to mobile view, so more important to have proper read/unread differentiation.)

**Right panel:**
4. When going to Messages or Reports tab by default show the top most record.
5. Need more distinction between received messages and sent messages. Border colors and reverse the position to be more like iOS, Hangouts.
6. Color code "Received", "Sent", "Pending" as seen in screenshot (carry this over to Reports tab as well, with "Scheduled" as grey, but same border styling)
7. Message text area and send button fixed at the bottom of the browser window
8. Show character count for composing a message
9. Show new sent message immediately at the bottom of the conversation

**I am adding these two:**
10. Lester is also working on an updated styling for the "Unread messages below", details to come
11. Contact name at top. This is necessary because there is no indication of who the conversation is with in the mobile view or if in full view and the selected contact in left pane is scrolled out of view. Lester is working on the styling for this, but in the meantime I think it should be fixed to the top of the right content pane, matching the styling of the compose box, and contain the same contact info as the left pane plus phone number. I think we should avoid putting this in the blue bar since we should leave that for the eventual filters and search box.
eg

Marc Abbyad (+14165558080)
District Name › Health Facility › Village Name

title: Status filters
body:
Currently the status filter includes the following options:
- Any Status
- Valid Only
- Invalid Only

We should update the list to represent verified/unverified as well. There are many ways to represent this: multi vs single select, individual vs combo status. The way that I'd like us to start is with single select and combo states so that each item visually represents a possible report state:
- Valid and Verified
- Valid and Unverified
- Invalid and Verified
- Invalid and Unverified

As a single select this would like this:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/4393282/5c713f94-4416-11e4-8ca3-499268dbf145.png)

Doing this as a multi select means that we cant show the selection in filter box, so I would start with this as a single select. I realize that this is less flexible/versatile, but will simplify the interface for our users. If we find users want multi select there we can add it later.

title: In the left pane: selecting an item makes the scroll offset visibly change
body:
If you scroll down to a non-zero `scrollOffset` in the left pane, and then select an item, the left pane visibly "jumps" up to `scrollOffset` zero and then back down to the original `scrollOffset`.

My best read of the situation: Angular is updating the content in the left pane every time you select an item, by asynchronously clearing and then replacing the content. This leave a window of time in which a repaint occurs, and the lack of content causes the `<div>` to automatically return to `scrollOffset` zero.

title: Add framework for running/storing analytics-like anonymous statistics
body: Add support for computing and caching anonymous statistics, which can later be sent back to Medic via SMS or HTTP if the user opts-in during setup. This issue doesn't (yet) include the actual data transmission – it's just the framework for computing and locally storing the "phone home" data. The framework should allow us to easily add procedures for computing new data elements, and should handle the details of scheduling when / how often the computation should be run. This'll likely end up in the `medic-api` codebase.

title: Profile sentinel, develop performance improvement and refactor plan
body:
Sentinel is too slow. No, seriously, it's way too slow. You can see this in action if you look at the `medic-data` continuous integration scripts, specifically the `demos-diy` script/dataset. It's taking nearly an hour to process 2-3k records; ideally, we could process 5k records in about 10-20 seconds.

Walk through the medic-sentinel code base, take notes, and develop a theory in writing (e.g. in a gist) that explains why sentinel is so slow. Then, if time permits, sketch out a strategy for fixing it.

title: Support localization and internationalization throughout the web application

Caveat: we already have an in-form localization system, plus an app_settings based localization system for portions of the application and automatic/scheduled SMS. We've heard from the product team that they'd like the translations to be editable _at runtime_, i.e. without requiring the application's source code and/or an application push/update.

title: Figure out how to accept data from ODK mobile data collection tools
body:
Allow data sent from ODK to be received by `medic-webapp`. For the time being, we can assume that (i) the ODK form is limited to integer, numeric, string, and date/timestamp fields; (ii) we have a suitable hand-built form definition already built that matches the ODK form; and (iii) that the ODK mobile app has a mobile data connection available to it.

This is a first small step toward interoperating with existing smartphone apps. That interoperability will take some project pressure off of our next-generation form/smartphone tools and allow us to take our time and do a good job.

title: Allow Medic OS to run on an existing Linux system (toward multiple-project instances on EC2)
body:
This issue is a first step toward Linux containers and/or Docker support, ultimately aimed at supporting multiple projects on a single EC2 instance.

During the `medic-os` build, we should create a single `.tar.xz` file containing a `README` and a general-purpose startup script suitable for BSD and/or SysV style init scripts. This tarball would be usable on any Linux system or distribution, and would use `chroot` to isolate itself from the rest of the system. This image could then be adapted in to a Linux Containers (LXC) image that'd be usable with Docker and plain Amazon Linux / RHEL EC2 instances.

3. Code complexity - it's confusing to have the two analytics modules included in a completely different way
4. UI inconsistency between the two analytics modules.

title: Use angularjs includes rather than dust includes
body:
In inbox.html we're using dust includes for angular templates and modal dialogs, eg:

```
{>"partials/modal_send_message.html"/}
...
<script type="text/ng-template" id="/partials/reports.html">
  {>"partials/reports.html"/}
</script>
```

This bundles all the templates into one html file which can't be cached so it has to be shipped to the user every page load. Instead, if we use an angular include they will be requested as individual files which can be cached, eg:

```
<ng-include src="'templates/partials/modal_send_message.html'"></ng-include>
```

For this we need to include the templates as attachments in the `kanso.json`, and include a route for templates in the `rewrites.js`.

Some templates will also need to be modified so where we used to have escaping like `{~lb}{~lb}contact.key[1]{~rb}{~rb}"` we can now use `{{contact.key[1]}}`.

Any javascript initialisation must now be invoked with the `onload` attribute on the include, rather than in the init of the controller.

This change will make the code a little cleaner, and the page a little quicker to load the second time around.

title: Medic OS: Allow bind ports and/or IPs to be specified at launch in a portable way
body: When two or more copies of Medic OS are run as a chroot application or in a Linux container, we'll need to ensure that they don't try to bind the same IP/port combination. Provide a way for Medic OS to discover and apply port and/or IP binding instructions. Ideally, this will be compatible with the way tools like Docker do it, _and_ will be usable on Medic OS hosts that have their own kernel (e.g. the ISO on VMware, or Xen on EC2).

title: Make visual layer changes to Kanso-based configuration screens
body:
Split off from #712.

We've decided to develop all new configuration screens on the AngularJS code base, in order to take the job on bit by bit over time. These new screens will use the inbox's visual layer. In order to maintain as much visual continuity as possible during the transition period, we're planning to restyle the older Kanso-based screens – they'll use the new tab-bar/header and top-level navigation.

We realize this won't be perfect. Some top-level functionality may not be identical to the main app.

title: Medic Transport: Refactor method of storing driver state
body: Currently, driver state is attached as a property of each driver in transport. As Dave pointed out, this could go horribly wrong if a driver implementation uses a private property of the same name. I couldn't come up with an elegant solution to this in the transport, so I simply moved the responsibility of storing state to the driver objects with get_state and set_state methods added to the driver prototype. On one hand this puts more work on the driver implementation, but on the other hand it improves upon state handling, in my mind crucially, by allowing each driver implementation the flexibility to deal with its own state (while maintaining transports' status updating mechanism).

title: kanso push fails with minify flag
body:
Kanso push fails with minify, this causes the auto-push to market to fail during builds.

```
kanso push --minify http://admin:123qwe@localhost:5984/medic
```

This appears to be a bug in node and/or uglifyjs. The push fails during an uglifyjs call on line 17 in packages/modules/build/attachment.js:

```
return pro.gen_code(ast);   // compressed code here
```

A stack trace shows the last call within node:

Trace
    at Object.exports.error (/Users/mandric/local/lib/node_modules/kanso/lib/logger.js:106:13)
    at process.<anonymous> (/Users/mandric/local/lib/node_modules/kanso/lib/logger.js:140:13)
    at process.emit (events.js:95:17)
    at process._fatalException (node.js:272:26)
Error: Maximum call stack size exceeded
Failed

Increasing the stack size works on my mac:

```
node --stack_size=100000 ~/local/lib/node_modules/kanso/bin/kanso push --minify http://admin:123qwe@localhost:5984/medic
```

Noticed uglifyjs was pretty old in the modules package (1.2.2).  When I upgraded it to latest (2.4.16) I get a different error which also is related to node:

Trace
    at Object.exports.error (/Users/mandric/local/lib/node_modules/kanso/lib/logger.js:106:13)

title: Create lucene query generation library
body:
To avoid string concatenation and potential injection issues, create a library which generates the query string and escapes parameters. Possible apis include prepared statements, object mapping, or builder pattern.

Java based builder: http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_7_1/core/org/apache/lucene/util/QueryBuilder.html
Lucene escaping: http://lucene.apache.org/core/2_9_4/queryparsersyntax.html#Escaping%20Special%20Characters

Publish the library, then use internally for Reports querying.

title: Check permissions in configuration controllers

Ensure a non-admin can't POST or PUT changes.

title: New phone numbers in Cameroon fail validation
body:
Several months ago an extra digit was added to all phone numbers in Cameroon. These updated numbers are not recognized as valid in the facilities list, not sure if it has been updated in libphonenumber yet.

All cell phones are now prefixed by a 6, all landlines prefixed by a 2. For instance +23750635999 is now +237650635999 (country code is 237).

Ideally these two numbers would be seen as equivalent in the webapp. That probably can't be done in libphonenumber, but for us we can assume that all numbers in the system are mobile numbers using the prefix 6, not 2.

title: Sort out how to keep libphonenumber up to date
body:
It is critical that libphonenumber is kept up to date otherwise we start rejecting valid numbers and messages à la #802.

Furthermore it's critical that all our services use the same version of libphonenumber otherwise we could fail validation in strange and poorly handled ways.

Currently medic-webapp uses a custom build of libphonenumber for kanso, and medic-transport uses a [third party package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/libphonenumber). Unfortunately this package isn't updated regularly and is currently about 6 months out of date.

Firstly get both transport and webapp using the same package, which should be an npm package as transport isn't based on kanso.

Secondly make sure the npm package can be regularly updated, either by getting commit and publish permissions, or by branching and creating our own npm package. This package should be updated as part of the release process.

title: Filter bar updates
body:
Based on feedback from UX testing, we should clean up the filter bar. There are a couple of quick things we can do to help now, as shown in the screenshots below.
- **Left align the filters:** Less of an issue in Reports' mobile view since they take up the whole bar in mobile view, but noticeable if in Tablet view or in the Contacts tab.
- **Clear filter:** From testing the "clear filters" button was not clearly understood. Recommendation is to keep it close to the filters and use the "undo" with the tooltip `Reset Filters`.
- **Clutter and confusion with the rightmost icons:** Fix would be to hide less used functions under hotdog. For Contacts tab, that would be Import and Export. For Reports there is only one button for now, but may as well put it under hotdogs for consistency. As for using two hotdogs one under the other, @diannakane thinks this will just reinforce the concept of contextual options. We will leave the Add icons where they are for now until further UX testing.
- **Back Button:** looks too much like a filter - restyle like other buttons
- **Search field:** functionality was not clear using a pencil. Use search icon with dropdown like the other filters, and keep its existing dropdown functionality as is.

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/6712697/5736a80c-cd64-11e4-8d16-f0201072101f.png)

We are also looking at the potential of moving filters to a tray that would slide out from the left, but that will not be for several months as we want to do some more UX testing. These light(er)weight changes should serve us very well until then.

title: In demo/preload data: ensure all messages ship in the 'sent' status
body:
Currently, when a user plugs a GSM modem in to a DIY installation, the system attempts to send all pending messages. This has the unfortunate effect of (probably) spamming some poor person in the British Virgin Islands, since we're no longer using invalid phone numbers (due to libphonenumber validation).

If we ship the demo/preload messages as `sent`, this won't happen and everyone will be happy.

title: Update Contact Types Filter
body:
The Contact Types filter should be split up into People and Places, still as a single filter. 

Example shown here in screenshot:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/6721775/45e01668-cda7-11e4-9033-d4939e2fe5e5.png)

Places have user defined types (Districts, Health Centers, Catchment Areas) whereas People don't have explicit types (yet). For now it would be useful to split Persons up by those that are Primary Contacts for a Place and those that are not.

Doing this will let us do more precise filtering. For example, to show only CHWs you can select Primary Contacts and Catchment Areas only. We can experiment with implicit types in the filter list during our next UX testing - by which point we may actually have other Person relationship to handle anyway.

title: 910 associate records with people
Namespace report fields
body:
Parsed report fields are currently stored directly on the doc which means they can conflict with reserved properties. For example. a form with a `contact` field would be overwritten when sentinel assigns a contact. Refactor this so that all form fields are stored in a specific property.

For bonus points we can also store some meta data about the field such as the type and the label then we save some effort when rendering the row because we don't need to look up the configuration again.

title: Fix for #925: tag HTTP requests with their update target
body:
An alternative approach to (https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/pull/955) for fixing #925.

This adds a new parameter for HTTP requests made through the
`HttpWrapper` service - `updateTarget`.  Current options for
`updateTarget` are `filter`, `left` and `right`, referring to different
sections of the UI which an HTTP request might update on successful
completion.

When the user navigates to different states, the `stateChangeStart`
listener selectively cancels pending HTTP requests depending on the old
and new states.

There are three tests which are broken by this commit.  They check that
the callback functions are working by testing that the error callbacks
are executed for cancelled requests.  This commit changed the behaviour
of the rest canceller from calling `resolve()` on request promises, to
instead calling `reject()`.  This seems to be better bahaviour, as it
prevents the deliberately-cancelled requests from being handled as
errors, but it is not clear to me how the tests should be modified to
reflect this change in behaviour.

@garethbowen please review

title: Automate building of DIY installer
body:
The DIY installer is currently built on a Windows machine with a mix of manual and scripted steps. We should automate this build process and publish an exe whenever any component or subproject gets updated.

The main repo is [medic/medic-msi](https://github.com/medic/medic-msi), subprojects are:
- [medic/medic-launchpad](https://github.com/medic/medic-launchpad)
- [abbyad/vmware-helper](https://github.com/abbyad/vmware-helper)
- [abbyad/winsw](https://github.com/abbyad/winsw)

Additional binaries are currently kept locally, but should be loaded at build time. We can host these files on S3.

I am testing a build on an EC2 Windows Server 2012 AMI, but ideally this could be run using a CI platform. Otherwise we can schedule a task on the EC2 instance.

---
# Steps to automation:

```
[x] install jenkins
[x] automate build: abbyad/vmware-helper
[x] automate build: abbyad/winsw
[x] automate build: medic/medic-launchpad
[x] automate build: medic/medic-msi`
  [x] build `.msi` file
  [x] build NSIS installer `.exe`
  [x] publish built `.exe` to S3
[x] commit jenkins config to version control
[x] document windows server setup in relevant git repo
[x] allow config of `medic-os` version when launching a `medic-msi` build
```

title: [api] Trailing slash on `COUCH_URL` causes missing login screen
body:
# Recreate
1. Specify COUCH_URL env var for `api` with a trailing slash, e.g.:
   
   ```
   COUCH_URL=http://admin:pass@localhost:5984/medic/
   ```
2. browse to `http://localhost:5988/medic/login`
3. observe the error:
   
   ```
   {"error":"not_found","reason":"missing"}
   ```
# Expected behaviour

Adding an extra slash to the `COUCH_URL` is an easy mistake to make.  It would be great if `api` could cope with this rather than confounding me.
# Notes
## Workarounds
### Fix your `COUCH_URL`

remove the trailing slash:

```
COUCH_URL=http://admin:pass@localhost:5984/medic
```
### Use a different URL

Add an extra slash to the URL you're trying to access:

```
http://localhost:5988/medic//login
```
## Suggested Fix

In `db.js`, strip trailing slash from `COUCH_URL` when it is initially read from `process.env`:

`var couchUrl = process.env.COUCH_URL;
if (couchUrl) {
  var parsedUrl = url.parse(couchUrl);`

e.g.

```
couchUrl = couchUrl.replace(/\/$/, '');
```

title: Enketo: Code cleanup, cached conversion to JSON
body:
As a first step toward an internal forms API, we need to create a (form-type-specific, cached) JSON version of Enketo's XML-formatted report (read: "form submission"). We need this because: (1) we agreed that removing all bare references to `doc.fields` and replacing them with accessors was too big of a task to take on all at once; (2) in the final API, a field accessor shouldn't have to parse the full XML report every time a field is read programmatically; and (3) we need a way for (at least a subset of) fields to be easily-accessible from CouchDB views.

One big upside to this approach: if this cached JSON is placed in `doc.fields`, most existing backend code and views that access doc.fields directly (e.g. in medic-sentinel and medic-api) should work as-is.

We'll file a follow-up issue, including some draft documentation/prototypes, for construction of a proper forms API that wraps this, then a big search/replace/refactor to use it instead of direct references to `doc.fields`. The cached copy will remain so that (a) views continue to function, and (b) programmatic accesses to commonly-used fields are fast.

title: API: Path to login assets is sensitive to current working directory
body: The login page is breaking in production due to `medic-api` being sensitive to the value of `process.cwd()`. If the current working directory is not equal to the enclosing directory for `server.js`, things break: ``` shell dave@aircrash (~/medic-api) $ node server.js &>/dev/null & [2] 58497 dave@aircrash (~/medic-api) $ curl http://localhost:5988/login Redirecting to /login/ dave@aircrash (~/medic-api) $ fg node server.js >&/dev/null ^C dave@aircrash (~/medic-api) $ cd .. dave@aircrash (~) $ node medic-api/server.js &>/dev/null & [2] 58500 dave@aircrash (~) $ curl http://localhost:5988/login {"error":"not_found","reason":"no_db_file"} ``` We're seeing this on Medic OS too, because `gardener` sets the current working directory to `working_dir/$UUID`, which is two levels above `server.js`. I was able to hack it into working on `alpha.dev` by doing this at the top: ``` js process.chdir(path.join(process.cwd(), 'node_modules', 'medic-api'));` ``` We should probably figure out the path to `server.js` at startup, and then do something along the lines of `process.chdir(path.dirname(path_to_server_dot_js))`.

title: Revoke blob Object URLs when forms are discarded
body:
> Each time you call [`createObjectURL()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/URL/createObjectURL), a new object URL is created, even if you've already created one for the same object. Each of these must be released by calling [`URL.revokeObjectURL()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/URL/revokeObjectURL) when you no longer need them. Browsers will release these automatically when the document is unloaded; however, for optimal performance and memory usage, if there are safe times when you can explicitly unload them, you should do so.
> _https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/URL/createObjectURL_

^ We're not doing this - we might like to consider it.

title: [enketo] code review
body:
1. ~~Don't use tables for non-tabular data, and never use nested tables, eg: [edit-report.html](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/develop/templates/modals/edit_report.html#L9). This example should probably be an unordered list.~~
2. ~~Internationalise everything. It's almost as easy to add a translation directive, a key, and an entry in the translation file as it is to add a hardcoded English string. eg: [edit-report.html](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/develop/templates/modals/edit_report.html#L13)~~
3. ~~Use the standard spinner when loading content, not static text. eg: [edit-report.html](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/develop/templates/modals/edit_report.html#L12)~~
4. ~~Use angular instead of jQuery wherever possible. The two don't play well together, so minimise the use of jQuery as much as possible. eg: [edit-report.js](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/develop/static/js/controllers/edit-report.js#L218). Instead of using jQuery to show and hide, set a scope property (eg: `$scope.loading = true`) and then use `ng-show="loading"` on the loading spinner.~~
5. ~~Don't generate HTML in JavaScript, eg: [edit-report.js](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/develop/static/js/controllers/edit-report.js#L196). This is particularly prone to bugs and is hard to read. It's nicer, easier to test, easier to read, and easier to maintain to have MVC separation. As per the above example it would be better to set the list of available forms on the $scope, and then use the `ng-repeat` directive on an element to stamp out the templates.~~
6. ~~Don't use inline event registration, eg: [edit-report.js](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/develop/static/js/controllers/edit-report.js#L197). It's very hard to maintain. In the angular world you should use `ng-click="loadXmlFrom(...)"` instead. NB: this requires using `ng-repeat` from number 5 above.~~
7. ~~Don't use globals if possible, eg: [edit-report.js](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/develop/static/js/controllers/edit-report.js#L212). One exception is if this is a requirement of the enketo library but I can't see that it is in this case.~~
8. ~~Don't use `!important`, eg: [medic.less](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/develop/static/css/enketo/medic.less#L15). Unless the style you're overriding breaks this rule, you _never_ need to use it. Simply make your selector more specific than the one you're overriding and it'll take precedence.~~ -> Added to #1233
9. ~~Don't commit compiled code, eg: [enketo-core-medic-0.2.1.js](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/develop/static/enketo/js/enketo-core-medic-0.2.1.js). Ideally it would be published to a repo, and the installed via npm or bower. At the very least it should be checked out at build time and not committed.~~ filed as #1232

title: Tabs too small in mobile view
body:
On a mobile view the tabs are small enough to be difficult to press. Given the overflow strategy in #740, which is to remove the logo and `+` from mobile view, we will have enough space for larger tabs.

We should aim to have the widest tabs possible assuming 5 tabs in the top bar.

title: Disable or fix medic-sentinel transitions to allow Enketo forms to submit cleanly
body:
Currently, submitting a form using the modal-contained Enketo renderer produces "invalid" records, with a number of validation errors despite the presence of seemingly-appropriate data. Disable the medic-sentinel transitions to see if this prevents records from being marked as invalid (high priority), then figure out how to get Enketo and the medic-sentinel transitions to coexist peacefully (lower-priority).

![enketo-validation-errors](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/763977/9474047/0775ed96-4b13-11e5-96cf-a10ed67dd134.jpg)

title: Enketo: restyle all of the things
body:
Currently, the Enketo UI/UX and CSS isn't ideal. On the mid-iteration call, we talked about (i) restyling the report creation and report editing screens pre-demo; (ii) removing/resizing some of the buttons and making disabled/enabled states clearer; and (iii) potentially getting rid of the modal entirely and embedding Enketo in the right pane.

Items (i) and (ii) would be nice to have done pre-demo; item (iii) is probably discussion-only at this point.

title: Login screen: use the full viewport in mobile mode
body: On both Chrome 30.0 (OEM browser) and Chrome 44.0 (not Webview) on Android, the `/medic/login` page initially appears as scaled-down/zoomed-out content. We should adjust the CSS to make sure the login screen fills the full viewport in mobile mode.

Related to #1202, remove the logo when in mobile view to make use of the space.

We can wait to remove the `+` once we have the "submit report" implemented elsewhere.

title: Bring place filter improvements from 0.5+ to 0.4
body:
We have heard from users recently that the place filter is difficult to use in 0.4. It seems unsorted and difficult to navigate:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9528165/3bc4da26-4cc1-11e5-994a-73dcc439d6bb.png)

This has been updated and fixed, but has not been pushed to Release. Here is an example of the improved filter:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9528115/00996462-4cc1-11e5-8112-9b3206902847.png)

The Facilities to Contacts change in 0.5 may have made this updated filter possible, but if it is feasible to include this improved filter back in 0.4 then we should do this rather than wait for the 0.5 release.

title: SMS messages are sent in duplicates or are very delayed
body: Creating an issue for the modem work that @browndav has been doing to troubleshoot duplicate and delayed messages.

title: Multiple report submissions
body:
If you click submit on a form multiple times before it goes through then you can end with multiple reports in the Reports tab.

We should disable the submit button after submission, and show a spinner to indicate that something is happening until the modal disappears.

title: [enketo] Implement geolocation type
body:
The geolocation type works on Enketo, but not yet in our embedded offline mode.

This is how it shows up in Enketo on a touchscreen laptop, which hides the map, and field in question has `appearance="hide-input"` to hide the input fields:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9539634/2a1de0c2-4d22-11e5-99dc-2cd99dd9db78.png)

Our embedded version defaults to a text field:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9539626/074e6864-4d22-11e5-8fa8-af6b4c04714f.png)

title: support dot notation in schedule timestamp property configuration
body: We need this now especially since form field data is in the `fields` property.  Otherwise you can't reference form field data to generate schedules. See https://github.com/medic/medic-sentinel/blob/develop/lib/schedules.js#L78

title: [Contacts] Submit "new pregnancy" or other form from patient's profile
body:
Mobile app users will need to be able to submit reports about patients from their profile page in the Contacts tab. 

The "action bar" on the bottom would have a "submit report" button. With the current UX, this would open a modal with the list of relevant forms for the patient (1).  The selected form would then be completed with certain fields pre-populated. 

For example, on a woman's profile you may want to add a new pregnancy. This will open the "New Pregnancy" form with the XML:

```
        '<pregnancy id="ANCR" version="2015-08-28">
          <group_info>
            <person_note/>
            <g_patient_name>' + patient_name+ '</g_patient_name>
            <g_patient_id>' + _id + '</g_patient_id>
          </group_info>
...'
```

where the `patient_name` and `_id` are taken from the contact profile.

Currently the action bar for people is as follows:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9569654/30e3125a-4f3f-11e5-9b3e-776d14b26e25.png)

We could replace the "Message All" with "Submit Report" button using the report icon for now, and exact label text TBD.

---

(1) Showing the Relevant forms would make it easier to maintain the workflow for users. For instance a 5 year old boy would not have "Add pregnancy" as a form option. The rules for which form to show may be rather complex, so it may be better to show all forms for the first iteration and then break out more issues for the form display rules (eg Woman age 10 to 50, without an outstanding pregnancy)

title: [enketo] Associate sent report to User/Person
body:
This may be two issues, but combining the idea as one. Right now the sender is selected from a drop down on the Edit Report modal. The sender should be the currently logged in user, which needs to be associated to a Person. 
1. Associate User to Person: We could associate the User and Person by making sure they have the same phone number, but ideally, in the User creation/edit page we would select the associated Person for a User. 
2. Associate reports: All reports sent by the User should automatically show up as being sent from the Person.

title: Targets/Analytics for mobile app
body:
The mobile app has a Targets tab, which could likely be implemented within our current Analytics tab, renamed to Targets. This issue is a placeholder for requirements and discussion.

Here is the latest mockup of the values that need to be shown for the Targets tab:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9570405/af89842c-4f58-11e5-94a4-86aa960bc639.png)

The "This month" is the current calendar month, not a rolling month period.

@yembrick can assist with questions related to the calculations.

For our first deployment the non mobile app users will be viewing their dashboards in the standalone Analytics webapp, not the Analytics tab.

title: [enketo] Include via npm/browserify/bower
body: Currently enketo code is included in `medic-webapp` as an unminified blob built from a tag of https://github.com/alxndrsn/enketo-core: https://github.com/alxndrsn/enketo-core/tags.  Instead we should be including it via browserify, bower or npm.

title: [enketo] datepicker is missing styles
body:
Previous to switching to `npm` management of enketo, the bootstrap datepicker source was modified to append datepickers as a subelement of `#enketo-widget-container`, which allowed datepicker-dropdown to be styled correctly.

There should be a way to style these correctly without modifying bootstrap-datepicker.

Also, from #1201 it is requested that `!important` is not used in style directives.  This may be possible as part of this ticket.

title: Clean up enketo bundling
body:
1. ~~Remove duplicated fonts~~
2. ~~move enketo fonts to static/fonts~~
3. ~~make sure fonts are included in app cache~~
4. ~~move enketo XSL to static/xsl~~
5. ~~make sure XSL files are included in app cache~~
6. ~~Bundle the enketo js into inbox.js~~
7. Remove the enketo specific grunt tasks and merge these into the type specific grunt tasks, eg: `grunt browserify` not `grunt browserify:enketo`
8. ~~Remove `/static/enketo` directory~~

title: Android URL settings error hides Save button
body:
1. Use the unbranded app
2. Type in an incorrect URL
3. Hit Save and a helpful error should show up
4. Change the URL to a correct one

You should now be able to hit save again, but I've had cases where the save button was completely obscured by the error message. It seems to be a little random as sometimes the error message will disappear when I start changing the URL.

We have a lot of unused vertical real estate here, so I think we should just show the error inline in the page rather than floating it over the button.

title: Reports list not updated when enketo forms submitted or edited
Assign a different schedule based on a form field value
body: We will want to have a different schedule if a pregnancy registration is determined to be high risk. This will be determined by fields within the registration form (eg `danger_signs` is not empty). This may be currently possible with the rules, but we need to confirm.

title: Open form directly from task list
body: In order to streamline the task-to-form process, we should have a task type which opens the associated form directly from the task list. This means that clicking on that task in the left pane shows the Enketo form in the right pane.

title: Show Enketo form in the right pane
body: Part of a larger UX refactor, we want to show the Enketo form in the right pane of the webapp, instead of the modal. This will make more sense with the rest of the UX refactor issues to come.

title: Forward compatibility: Ensure that implementing Enketo localization sometime in the future is pain-free
body: We should pass the users locale in to the enketo form rendering so the forms can be localised.

title: Refactor EditReportCtrl for unit testing and maintainance
body:
The EditReportCtrl has the Enketo rendering code embedded in it. This is bad because it cannot be reused, is outside of the concern of the controller, and controllers are difficult to unit test.

Pull as much of the Enketo code out of the controller and into an Enketo service as possible. Then write unit tests.

title: Generate tasks from any report
body:
The TaskGenerator picks out ANC registrations with or without LMP to generate tasks. This means it only works for the ANC use case. It's also not configurable enough because it only allows up to two registration forms, and there's no option to have non-registration reports generate events (eg: follow ups).

Pass all reports to nools and let the configuration decide which to generate schedules from.

title: [enketo] jr:// media URLs should be processed before form is added to DOM
body:
Currently the media URLs are processed _after_ the form is added to the DOM, which causes error logs such as:

> `GET jr://video.mp4 net::ERR_UNKNOWN_URL_SCHEME`

title: Show right pane content full screen in mobile/tablet view
body:
Part of the larger UX refactor mentioned in #1243, in the mobile view all right pane content should be shown "full screen". 

**Mobile/Tablet view:** Hide the top bars when viewing the right pane. 
**Desktop view:** In desktop view the right pane would **remain as is**.

Here are some examples of the right pane in mobile/tablet view:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9688588/1357e694-52fe-11e5-886b-803bf12c2350.png)

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9688480/6d12512a-52fd-11e5-99a7-3238d592f1b3.png)

Followup issues will be posted for content of the right pane given the context.

title: Update to Enketo navigation buttons
body:
From feedback from several testers, we will not be showing the `submit` button until you have reached the end of the form. That means showing only `back` and `next` as such:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9688431/2eb94122-52fd-11e5-8910-c8fe4a70eb68.png)

When the end of the form is reached, instead of a `next` button it would show the `done` button in its place. The `back` button should be disabled when on the first page of the form.

title: Android container: Support screen reorientation
body:
We used the Tecno Y4's "lock orientation" feature for the demo. Currently, turning the device from portrait to landscape mode (apparently) triggers a full page reload, which turns the screen white for a relatively long period of time and makes the application appear (okay, actually-be) unresponsive.

We should be able to switch between portrait and landscape mode on a Tecno Y4 Chromium 30 Webview without major UX disruption.

title: [Tasks] Icons and styling for individual tasks
body:
Here is a mockup of tasks with related icons:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9690078/3e05cc4e-5308-11e5-8603-ca4c7bfec26b.png)
**Primary icons:** On the left, relate to the task type. Ideally it would be possible to upload a new set of icons to choose from for each project.

**Secondary icons:** On the right, may relate to a property of the task's entity e.g. the patient a task relates to has danger signs, so show as a high risk pregnancy.

**Secondary label:** The text next to the alert icon should be configurable separately from the choice of the icon. Ideally it would be possible to set the text and color of that secondary text.

_Note that icons may overlap with the ones show in #1230._

title: Remove logo from Tablet view
body: As done with the mobile view in #1218, remove the Medic logo from the "tablet view" (401-767px wide). Otherwise the logo appears/disappears when rotating between landscape and portrait on phones used by projects (eg Tecno Y4).

title: Larger tab buttons
body:
We have received feedback from many testers that the buttons and text are too small. The ones that seem to be most problematic so far are top level tabs.

@garethbowen's suggestion was to divide the available space for the visible tabs.

title: Remove `+` from top bar
body:
The actions available in the `+` in the top bar should be moved to the "floating action bar" in their proper context.

**Submit report:** 
Practically speaking, most reports will be triggered from a task, or from a patient profile. For generic reports not related to a person, place, or tasks, you can `Create New Report` using the button in the action bar in the Reports tab shown here:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9690431/4f700ec0-530a-11e5-9148-00e89dd1eaae.png)

**Send message:** 
It is currently possible to send new messages via a button in the sub top bar of the Messages tab. Ideally that would be moved to follow the same pattern as with _Reports_. Since the Messages tab is not used in the mobile app yet it is suitable to leave it as is for now.

title: [Contacts] Show search field when tab is loaded
body:
Show the full input field on the Contacts tab in mobile view. 

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/10619625/a015b2a4-7744-11e5-855b-5cc8743b6270.png)

If we do this for all search fields this will have unintended consequences in the Reports tab where the filter bar is already full of filters. We could show the search bar in full only when there is sufficient space, and collapse to the button version if there isn't. Given that this is a requirement only for the Contacts tab, we can take the approach that is most efficient (eg only have the full search bar in the Contacts tab, leave the field as is in the Reports tab).

title: [Contacts] Remove place and type filters based on user role
body: In order to keep the workflow and UX cleaner, we have been asked to remove some filters. By making the visibility of the individual filter role based, we solve this problem and also have the benefit of postponing discussion related to the filters until we have feedback from users using them.

title: [Contacts] Default filters per role
body:
As alluded to in #1257, the default filter for the Contacts tab should be configurable by role. 

For our immediate needs, the mobile CHW user would need the filter to show only the "Families":
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9691645/adac9e8e-5311-11e5-9b8c-b58d938f5bc2.png)

title: [Contacts] Move add place and person buttons
body:
Based on feedback to clean up the UX and workflow for mobile users we should move the add place/person buttons to the floating action bar. 
- **Add Place** is within the left pane, see image below.
- **Add Person** is done in the action bar for the place, when it is being viewed in the right pane. This means that a person must be associated to a place. Issue related to this yet to come.
- Prevent the deletion of a place if there are people associated to it. The delete icon should be disabled, and/or if clicked should show an alert message explaining that the people would need to be deleted first.

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9690654/c834f6c6-530b-11e5-9e05-d5df0a4c655c.png)

title: [Contacts] Place profile updates
body:
The updated UX for the "Place" should include three sections:

The profile contains three sections:
- **Tasks:** All tasks related to the place or any of its people. Clicking on any of these tasks would open the task's form.
- **People:** All the people associated to the place. Clicking on the person would open the person's profile page.
- **Reports History:** a running list of all of the reports related to the place, but not the ones for the people associated to the place. This is shown outside of the viewport, but is available within the same profile page. Clicking on a report would show the same view as if it were selected from the Reports tab.

Here is an example for the place level called "Family":
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9692167/4ede1dfc-5315-11e5-9f8a-b4f9fc43da9c.png)

title: [Contacts] Person profile updates
body:
Three sections for the person profile page:
- **Base info**: Info from the person creation form. Ideally we could select which subset of info is being shown here since we want this to be compact so that the Tasks are not below the fold.
- **Tasks**: All tasks related to this person. Clicks through to the task's form.
- **Reports History**: All reports submitted about this person. Clicking through brings you to the report's view.

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9692359/8588c9fa-5316-11e5-9a62-b75077fb98ca.png)

title: [Contacts] Action bar updates
body:
As seen in #1261 and #1262, the action bar has updated actions:

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9692644/691ac9f6-5318-11e5-90fa-6310f0b52659.png)
- **Call**: In mobile/tablet view this should be a link to call the primary phone number for the contact (eg `href="tel:+16505551234"`) which we need to then handle in medic-android. In desktop view this can be either disabled, or replaced with the SMS action.
- **Add**: Opens a list of all the possible reports that can be submitted for this person/place. This would also include adding more people to a place, send SMS to the contact, and SMS all where appropriate.
- **Edit**: Edit the current person/place's basic info.
- **Delete**: As expected, deletes the person or place, but only if there are no people/places associated to it. If there are those must first be deleted or reassigned.

title: [Reports] Move top level tab to beneath Menu icon
body:
As seen below, the Reports tab should not be accessible as a top level tab. This is to streamline the top level options and avoid confusion with users that rarely need to see the reports tab - which will increasingly be the case for certain types of users.

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9692952/a39e29f4-531a-11e5-9f2f-95067ed2d5c1.png)

Given that this requirement is likely to change from one project to another, and even for different types of users within a deployment, we likely want the choice of tabs shown under the Menu icon to be configurable by user role.

_Edit: Changed "settings" to "menu" icon for clarity._

title: [android] Test back button functionality
body:
This is a placeholder to retest the back functionality on Android devices. 

We should determine if the use of the back button is working as expected in its current implementation (back in history until no more, then exit app) and if that is suitable for users.

With the refactored UX, an alternative would be to go "up/back" a level until you reach the top level tabs and then exit.

title: Submit reports related to a person or place
body:
We want to submit reports about a person (eg new pregnancy), or about a place (eg household survey). Currently, followup reports are based on `patient_id`, which is created with a registration form but has no connection to our new contacts.

We likely need to assign people and places a unique ID, and given that contact creation can happen offline, this ID probably needs to be a UUID. This ID could then be discreetly passed to any task and report related to the place/person, and submitted reports would then be associated to the contact.

Reports submitted about a person or place would then be shown on their profile, as described in #1261 and #1262.

title: [android] Start call from webapp
[Tasks] Configurable start and end time
body: Tasks are now shown as soon as they pass a rule. We would want the task to be shown only during a particular time window. This way, a task could be configured to only show up 2 days ahead of an event, and disappear when no longer relevant (eg no point doing the 48hr followup 2 weeks later).

title: [android] improve app URL validation
body: https://github.com/medic/medic-android/issues/9

title: map project form names to internal representation names
body:
Calculations are much easier when the source of the data is the same, be it Spreadsheets or Postgres.

So when each project decides to have a different ANC registration form name (e.g. ANCR, R, P, a Nepalese character that I can't reproduce), yet the fields are pretty much the same, then we get into a situation where our calculations should work but won't due to missing pointers/tables/sheets.

One easy solution is to create a view like `formview_ANCR` and simply `SELECT  * FROM formview_$$$$` where `$$$$` is the project's form name.

But then a recent project has started using reserved form names for different reasons, so maybe instead of `formview_ANCR` we might want `useview_ANCR` so that there is no name collisions between what analysis wants to read from and what projects want to write to.

Then we create a mapping between `formview_XXX` and `useview_YYY` in some table config. Some PL/pgSQL function would read the table config and generate a `useview` for each `formview`.

This covers the 75% use case. However there are some instances where `ANCR` is actually a combination of both `P` and `R` as a union, and one instance where `ANCR` is actually a combination of `P` and `R` as a partial union (`P` + `R` where `R` patient is not in `P`). The mapping might need to be able to define custom SQL or PL/pgSQL rather than just one `formview` mapped onto a `useview`.

title: Access person/place profile's fields from within a report
body:
When starting a new form about a person or place we need to access a variety of fields from their profile. This is used for instance to prepopulate an ID field so that the form is attached to the appropriate person. From a Task the prepopulation is possible using the task rule. We need a way to do this for forms initiated from the person/place's profile page. 

Currently the `place_id`/`patient_id` can be passed to a report. We also want to use other fields such as Name, DOB, LMP, EDD, or any field configured for that project's profiles, so it makes sense to consider the work done in #1260 before tackling this.

This is a followup to #1060 and #1185.

Some of the differences I have noticed so far:

title: Enketo: now() and today() give different results, specification says they should return identically-formatted results
body:
The Openrosa specification lists `now()` as being "same as `today()`", but currently one of them returns a Unix epoch timestamp and one returns a Gregorian-formatted date/timestamp. These functions should both return strings that are encoded in the same way. If we need a Unix-style timestamp, we should probably extend the API in a way that doesn't conflict with existing functions.

Split off from #1334, which was moved to Ready with to-do list item #2 still remaining.

title: Populate the patient_id/place_id fields within a form group

            <value>Watch this!</value>
          </text>
        </translation>
      </itext>
      <instance>
        <treatments id="CODE">
...
```

title: Incorrect XPath evaluation without parentheses
body:
Some conditions have unexpected behaviour with some calculation and relevant values.

For instance, the following correctly evaluates to false:
`(0 > 0) and (false != "true")`

but this incorrectly evaluates to true in Medic, but not in Enketo proper:
`0 > 0 and false != "true"`

Given the difference in behaviour between Enketo and Medic, I suspect this is related to our xpath evaluator.

title: Allow client-side caching of static resources
body:
The most suitable approach to this seems to be to serve an `etag` header from either `medic-api` or `nginx` containing the hash of the file's contents.

We assume that any asset change will result in a ddoc change, so we should re-calculate hashes when a ddoc change is detected.  Alternatively we could just calculate hashes on `api` startup, and assume that `api` will be bounced when the ddoc changes, at least in prod(?).

Probably this could be applied to anything in `static/dist` (or perhaps just anything in `static`).

title: Task generator performance
body:
Every interaction with the TaskGenerator gets all the contacts and reports from the database, compiles the task rules, and generates the tasks. This is now proving a performance bottleneck.

Some ideas to improve performance:
1. cache results in the task generator and expire the cache every x minutes
2. cache results in the task generator and listen for changes to reports or contacts to expire the cache
3. use a changes listener and keep nools running and provide new facts to the engine on change

Currently the user provided configuration has to decide whether tasks are emitted based on the relevant date. It might be better to have the nools configuration emit all tasks and filter in the task generator. That way items to show could change over time without rerunning the rules which would be particularly useful for option 3.

title: Remove the SettingsP service
body:
We have a Settings and a SettingsP service, the latter is a Promise based version of the former. The promise version doesn't use the cache so it regresses on #1174.

Fix this by only have one Settings service and ensuring it uses the cache. The optimal solution is to use promises only but this will be a large refactor. If this isn't possible in a reasonable time, support both in one service by returning a promise, and calling a callback (if provided).

It might also be necessary or at least good to rework the Cache service to be promise based.

Error watching for changes on the design doc e
Error watching for changes on the design doc e
Uncaught (in promise) e
Error watching for changes on the design doc e
```

It looks like pouchdb expects couchdb should timeout cleanly after 25000 but from [the docs](https://couchdb.readthedocs.org/en/1.4.x/changes.html), if a heartbeat is supplied couchdb ignores the timeout.

> heartbeat: Period in milliseconds after which an empty line is sent in the results. Only applicable for longpoll or continuous feeds. Overrides any timeout to keep the feed alive indefinitely.

On my local machine without nginx these requests remain pending forever which is why I suspect it's nginx that's doing the request cancellation.

Initially I thought this might be part of our replication issues ( #1341 ) but replication appears to work as expected so I think it just causes lots of unnecessary connections and confusing error messages.

The fix is to configure nginx to have a longer (infinite?) timeout on any longpoll request. Also consider patching pouchdb so the timeout header is only included when the heartbeat header is not.

title: Replace bower with npm
body:
We use both bower and npm in webapp which causes unnecessary complexity at build time. Switch all the bower dependencies to npm dependencies and `require` the modules so browserify compiles them in. This will make getting sourcemaps ( #1169 ) much easier.

Possible issues:
- Bower flattens the dependency tree so you only get one version of each library. Make sure `npm dedupe` is run as part of the build process which attempts to do a similar thing but less aggressively. Ensure that the final minified file size isn't too much larger than the previous inbox.js + dependencies.js.
- This will result in only a single js import (inbox.js) rather than dependencies.js and inbox.js. We initially split the files because of a bug in Chrome storing large files in the appcache. I think this bug only affected private browsing mode which isn't currently supported. If this is still an issue we can make a dependencies.js but having a separate js file that just requires all the libraries we don't call directly, and browserify that.

title: Unrecoverable 502 Bad Gateway if app is started when Garden is updating

If you start the app when Garden is updating, the app sees a 502 Bad Gateway error (from nginx?).  There is no refresh-link on this page, so user must force-close the app.

1. add a simple self-link to nginx error pages so that the user can try again easily
2. add error handling to the android client so any 5xx status codes display a status message and perhaps automatically retry

title: [android] No easy way to skip past a textarea
body:
In a normal textfield, you can press the `Go` key (equivalent to `<enter>` on a computer keyboard) to skip to the next field in an enketo form, without having to close the soft-keyboard.

In a `textarea`, the `CR` key is shown on the android keyboard instead of `Go`, which means there is no obvious way to get to the next field.
### Suggested fixes
1. remove _Notes_ field
2. change _Notes_ to a textfield
3. add a hovering _Next_ button after the caret in textfields on android
4. putting notes on a separate page might solve the issue
5. have a checkbox above the textarea to show/hide it (unchecked and field hidden by default

title: Warn users, or prevent them from using android app, when device date is set incorrectly
body:
A common problem reported by LG is that CHPs will swap SIMs or battery-out restart their phones, so losing the time & date settings.  When the app is restarted with a date far in the past, _Tasks_ will no longer be correctly calculated.

A suggested way to handle this is record the "previous start time" of the app.  When restarting, if the new start time is less than the last start time, show the user a warning, or block them from using the app.  E.g.

> Your phone's date is set in the past.  Reported date:
>   1 January 1970
> Please update the phone date.
> [ _ignore_ ] [ _exit_ ]

title: Replication performance: PouchDB may be downloading more docs than it needs to
body:
pouch is generating a query similar to this:

`/medic/_changes?timeout=25000&style=all_docs&heartbeat=10000&filter=medic%2Fdoc_by_place&_nonce=1450453351782`

the problem is in the `style` value:

> `style` _(string)_ – Specifies how many revisions are returned in the changes array. The default, `main_only`, will only return the current “winning” revision; `all_docs` will return all leaf revisions (including conflicts and deleted former conflicts).
> –_http://docs.couchdb.org/en/latest/api/database/changes.html_

Is there an obvious reason why pouch would need `all_docs` (as it does currently) instead of `main_only`?

title: Improve ng-repeat rendering?

>  If you are working with objects that have an identifier property, you should track by the identifier instead of the whole object. Should you reload your data later, `ngRepeat` will not have to rebuild the DOM elements for items it has already rendered, even if the JavaScript objects in the collection have been substituted for new ones. title: form metadata cannot be parsed on 0.6 systems
body:
Due to the switch from forms defined in JSON to forms defined in XML to support Enketo, the existing code to interpret couch data into one view per form cannot work for 0.6.

Here is the code which currently parses 0.4 JSON form metadata into relevant views:
https://github.com/medic/middleware/blob/master/postgres/formviews.sql#L37-L43

It expects a ddoc to contain `app_settings.forms.<formname>.fields`, which are currently a dictionary/object/hash by field name. The field name (key) is still required, obviously.

It expects `app_settings.form.<formname>.fields.<fieldname>.labels.short.en` to contain the field's English name as text. This is used as the column label for the form field in the form's view.

It expects `app_settings.form.<formname>.fields.<fieldname>.position` to have an integer. This integer sorts the fields so that the form view builder deterministically generates the same columns in the same order every time for any given form view. This is surprisingly important.

title: Detect when pouch has unsynced changes so we can have a simple sync status somewhere
body:
It would be useful, even if just for debug purposes, to be able to tell if everything in a user's pouchdb has been replicated into the cloud.

I was hoping that pouchdb replication would provide useful information. So far I've had a super quick look at the event handlers you can add to the replication call: http://pouchdb.com/api.html#replication

Unfortunately they don't seem massively useful by themselves. You effectively have `active`, `paused` and `change` to play with:
-  `change` fires _when a change has been replicated_.
- `active` and `pause` are switched between fairly regularly when pouch thinks it might have something useful to do but then realises for whatever reason it doesn't. 
- `pause` is the end state (since we are continuously replicating) regardless of whether we have changes that need to be duplicated.

Note that there is no obvious indication that you're offline, just that you're not currently actively replicating.

One possibility would be to make sure we funnel all our pouch db put calls through one wrapping function which keeps a list of all the document ids that pass through, and then remove them as they work their way through the change event handler. We could then bind that list (or a count of that list) to the UI and use it to display our sync indication.

title: XForm field with `calculate="today()"` gets wrong date in certain timezones
body:
A XForm field with `calculate="today()"` gets yesterday's date for computers in EST and PST, but the correct date for a computer in GMT.

Working theory is that the date value _in the current timezone_ is obtained for today at midnight GMT, which results in yesterday's date for Western timezones.

If the `today()` is used in a calculation (eg `decimal-date-time(today())`) it appears as expected. Also, today() seems to have different behaviour in Enketo proper, which maintains the time information.
## Sample form

```

  <h:head>
    <h:title>Test: today</h:title>
    <model>
      <instance>
        <test-today id="test-today" version="2016-02-05">
          <value/>
          <verification/>
          <note/>
        </test-today>
      </instance>
      <bind calculate="today()" nodeset="/test-today/value" type="string"/>
      <bind calculate="decimal-date-time(today())-decimal-date-time(../value)" nodeset="/test-today/verification" type="string"/>
      <bind nodeset="/test-today/note" readonly="true()" type="string"/>
    </model>
  </h:head>
  <h:body>
    <input ref="/test-today/note">
      <label>**today() set as ../value**: <output value=" /test-today/value "/>

**verify today() in calculation vs standalone value:**
decimal-date-time(today()) - decimal-date-time(../today/) = <output value=" /test-today/verification "/>
_should be 0_</label>

title: Minimise templated HTML
body:
Looks like the following ngTemplate options could be worthwhile:

> ### htmlmin
> 
> > Object containing [htmlmin options](https://github.com/gruntjs/grunt-contrib-htmlmin) that will _significantly_ reduce
> > the filesize of the compiled templates.
> 
> Without this, the HTML (whitespace and all) will be faithfully compiled
> down into the final `.js` file.  Minifying that file will only cut down
> on the _Javascript_ code, not the _HTML_ within the strings.
> 
> I recommend using the following settings for production:
> 
> ``` js
> htmlmin: {
>   collapseBooleanAttributes:      true,
>   collapseWhitespace:             true,
>   removeAttributeQuotes:          true,
>   removeComments:                 true, // Only if you don't use comment directives!
>   removeEmptyAttributes:          true,
>   removeRedundantAttributes:      true,
>   removeScriptTypeAttributes:     true,
>   removeStyleLinkTypeAttributes:  true
> }
> ```
> 
> If you are using SVG, please make sure you set `keepClosingSlash:true`
> 
> – https://github.com/ericclemmons/grunt-angular-templates#htmlmin

title: Postgres needs to support Contacts in a sane way
body:
Generally, contacts is JSON and could be parsed using Postgres JSON stuff into views. This would be broken down into a view for CHPs, a view for patients, a view for this or that other kind of contact.

However, it sounds like LG will need to add extra data for CHPs (if not other sorts of contacts), which would be best facilitated by making and populating a table. This would be node work.

Alternatively, make views of contacts could work if there is a table with primary key of UUID for storing only extra parameters. Then create a secondary view which combines this or that contacts view with the extra table information.

title: App doesn't handle authentication invalidating over time gracefully
body:
CouchDB authentication is only valid for a (configurable) small amount of time, which is refreshed on every request. I think the default is 10 minutes. If you leave your phone / browser for awhile and come back you will have lost that, and will need to reauthenticate.

Here for example. I opened the app on mah tecno, and then left it for 30 min or so. I then `grunt dev`'d to force a design doc change:

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/583851/13142900/2877392c-d638-11e5-9077-e953b0f3e175.png)

The most critical upshot of this is that replication can silently fail (in both directions) once you get into this state. For example, if I then try to change a contact on Cptn. Tecno. Everything looks fine on the phone, but in the log I get.

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/583851/13142939/6af750f2-d638-11e5-9eb1-c53d4481f84a.png)

There are two obvious solutions: 
- Have the couchdb authentication timeout as effectively infinite. I believe this may be what is happening with some clients now. It's not ideal.
- Have a log in modal that we pop up and use to refresh credentials
- Tell the user they have been logged out and then force a a page refresh
