title: Simplify medic specific XForm notation
body:
The goal of this issue is to simplify the customization needed to make XForms work within the webapp. We currently use some special notation within the XForm to make it work well with the webapp (eg to assign the form to a contact, or to display only certain fields in the Reports/History tab). 

Here is a proposal for some of the changes, which may help increase performance by reducing field duplication, reduce time to build forms, and make the data more easily accessible for exports as well as for calculations in task/target rules.
### `inputs` group

The fields in this group are currently populated automatically when the form is opened from a Contacts tab profile. Similarly, when form is opened from a Task the fields are populated by the task rule. When opening the form from Reports/History tab we cannot use the same inputs group and also hide it when it is prepopulated. The workaround includes having the patient or place info being selected in a separate group if not already populated, then coalescing these in the outputs. Eg:

``` xml
          <inputs>
            <patient>
              <_id/>
              <name/>
              <date_of_birth/>
            </patient>
          </inputs>
          <g_inputs>
            <_id/>
            <name/>
            <date_of_birth/>
          </g_inputs>
          <outputs>
            <patient_id/>
            <patient_name/>
            <patient_dob/>
            ...
          </outputs>
```

The suggestion here would be to use a `inputs/source` field so we can avoid the duplication and simplify the form creation.  `inputs/source` would be one of `contact`, `task`, `user`, with the later as the default if it is not set programmatically by via a profile or task. The resulting data model would be:

``` xml
          <inputs>
            <source>user</source>
            <patient>
              <_id/>
              <name/>
              <date_of_birth/>
            </patient>
          </inputs>
```

Aside from populating the source field we would need to check the `inputs/patient/_id` instead of `outputs/patient_id` when associating the report to the person. 
### Person, not Patient

We could also use this opportunity to use the more generic `person` rather than `patient` since reports are not always about patients (eg a report may be about a CHW as completed by their manager).
### Make all the fields accessible

We should assign all the field to json, not just the outputs section as done [here](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/167a812e2afc6be62d6b3424fe527cf9b9dc9a44/static/js/services/enketo.js#L233)

Right now we need to duplicate fields into the `outputs` section to have it in the `doc.fields`, which determines which elements are shown in the Reports/History tab, which are accessible programmatically from rules, and which are available for export. This can reduce performance due to extra fields, and makes it difficult to access the data that was initially omitted from the `outputs`. 

By default we would show all fields, and hide those that we don't want to show. This is currently possible with `tag="hidden"` in data model (https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/issues/1476). Nested fields are not shown elegantly right now because all the subfields are shown as JSON, but we can chose to hide these fields until we display them better via https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/issues/1473.

title: Make sure users eventually update their app
body:
If a user is presented with the update dialog and they hit cancel, there are no more (obvious) opportunities for them to install that update. Note that "install that update" really just means refresh the page.

This is probably important, since I imagine if we deploy an update we want people to be moved to it as quickly as is convenient.

It is also understandable that users can cancel the update dialog at that specific moment, as they may be in the middle of something.

This may require UX design.

Two options that Alex and I discussed:
- Storing if there is an unapplied update in the `$scope` and folding a refresh into the next action. For example, saving a form would save the form and then trigger a refresh.
- Storing if there is an unapplied update in the `$scope` and adding an idle timeout. For example, if you needed to refresh and were idle for more than 5min trigger a refresh.

Another that Estelle mentioned would be to re-popup the dialogue every N minutes if the update was not applied.

Note that as long as there is no unsaved data refreshes should be safe in any network situation.

title: Potential memory leak with our use of PouchDB
body:
I have created heap snapshots, dumps and CPU profiles of all this. I will upload them to drive once I have the bandwidth to do so, and link them here.

To reproduce:
- (potentially) connect to a remote host like lg-testing
- Clean your android install
- Configure the app to point to and log in as someone who has production-levels of data. I.e. more than demo on lg.dev
- Let the whole thing sync. Feel free to hang out on the about page, which should be doing nothing at all.
- Once the sync is complete, note that:
  -- The CPU is still doing a bunch of stuff. A pull from the profile I took looks like this:
  ![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/583851/13597765/493b1abe-e52b-11e5-85c3-c033295a2237.png)

title: Unbranded container, first-run URL input: Once an invalid URL is tested, subsequent valid URLs fail
body:
If I install the unbranded container and get the server address right the first time, I see a request to `/setup/poll` that results in an HTTP 200, and all is well.

If I purposely input a server name that exists but responds to `/setup/poll` with a 404, I'll be told that it's not a valid application URL. Great so far.

If I _then_ try a known-valid server name after the failure immediately above, it too gets flagged as invalid despite the fact that it's a real `medic-webapp` server. On the server side, I see an HTTP 401:

```
127.0.0.1 - - [11/Mar/2016:00:49:49 +0000] "GET /setup/poll HTTP/1.0" - - "-" "Dalvik/2.1.0 (Linux; U; Android 6.0.1; Nexus 6 Build/MMB29Q)"

==> /srv/storage/medic-core/couchdb/logs/couch.log <==
[Fri, 11 Mar 2016 00:49:49 GMT] [info] [<0.5997.0>] 49.xxx.xxx.220 - - GET /setup/poll 401
```

An easy workaround it to just uninstall and reinstall the APK, but we should figure out what credentials are riding along with that `/setup/poll` request, if any, that are leading to the 401.

title: Iterative steps can overlap in time causing redundancies
body:
I had the sleep interval set for 1 minute and doc size set to 3000.

The design doc didn't get pulled in until the very last set, so during the last iteration, all the XML data was being parsed and it took longer than 1 minute.

Meanwhile, the 1 minute timer went off to start the next iteration, which amazingly happened in parallel instead of waiting. Then that iteration, too, began parsing all the data.

In the end, this resulted in duplicate copies of all the parsed form data.

I need to block the next iteration timer from going off until the previous one is done. In fact, I didn't think this was possible but apparently it is.

title: Decision about dependency versioning
body:
Our current [`package.json`](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/develop/package.json) has a mix of `~` and `^` semvers in it. It is unclear how intentional or not this is.

We should:
- Pick a dependency strategy that will be obvious when you look at `package.json`, so that everyone easily keeps to the strategy
- Make is clear when we are deviating from the strategy and why, so that people don't think it's a "mistake" and fix it later (ie we're holding back this version for these reasons)
- Change `package.json` to fit this
## Option A: Loose versioning

_(use `^` as a default, if not note why)_

``` js
  "dependencies": {
    "angular": "^1.5.3",
    "jquery": "~2.1.4", // 2.2.x breaks enketo, see #1234
    "enketo-core": "git://github.com/enketo/enketo-core.git#4.5.5", // not yet on npm, see #5678
    "underscore": "1.8.3", // 1.8.4 has security issues, see #9012
  }
```
## Option B: Automatic patches

_(use `~` as a default, if not note why)_

``` js
  "dependencies": {
    "angular": "~1.5.3",
    "jquery": "~2.1.4", // NB: 2.2.x breaks enketo, see #1234
    "enketo-core": "git://github.com/enketo/enketo-core.git#4.5.5", // not yet on npm, see #5678
    "underscore": "1.8.3", // 1.8.4 has security issues, see #9012
  }
```
## Option C: Strict versioning

_(specific versions only )_

``` js
  "dependencies": {
    "angular": "1.5.3",
    "jquery": "2.1.4", // NB 2.2.x breaks enketo, see #1234
    "enketo-core": "git://github.com/enketo/enketo-core.git#4.5.5", // not yet on npm, see #5678
    "underscore": "1.8.3", // NB 1.8.4 has security issues, see #9012

```

title: Improve rendering performance for administrators on large data sets
body:
There are a few things that struggle to render quickly on my (beefy) laptop if you log in as an admin on a dataset the size of LG's (which is just forming, and presumably soon will be _much_ larger).

Currently we've disabled nools for administrators (ie they can't see CHP's tasks), as the massive amount of processing required for such a large dataset was causing huge browser freezes.

There are other issues. Search filters are especially noticeable, presumably because they have to load and render all contacts into the filter drop-downs. This is my network tab after doing a refresh, as admin, on the contacts page, on a server running locally using a PROD-sized DB:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/583851/14612066/3dc82cda-058d-11e6-88dd-16d594c6bae8.png)
41 of those mb are getting all the contacts, and about 10 of those seconds were (presumably) the search bar parsing and rendering after it had downloaded all of those contacts. The bandwidth issue (which tbf is made _much_ worse by the fact that when you work locally you don't have gzip enabled) will be dealt with in: _(a soon to be created and linked ticket)_

As I see it there are three ways to solve this problem:
- Optimise slow interactions so they perform much better with large datasets without changing the UI. Note that this might not be possible in some cases, i.e. we actually need to generate the DOM for all of the contacts for filtering
- Change each UI component that is slow to first have a filter for which CHP you wish to be. For example, step 0 of showing tasks would be to select a CHP, and then we would load their tasks. Or the contact filter would be changed to only allow listing high-level contacts (ie branches) or people / families for a specific CHP.
- Remove / change all interactions that are slow for admins (ie remove tasks, only show high level contacts such as branches) and then have a button that allows you to masquerade as a CHP _side wide_. Once you were a CHP you'd see the Tasks page and you'd see their tasks etc.

The third option may be the best, as it might be possible to just change one piece of code somewhere in the auth system, as well as a bit of UI changes (so that you know who you're masquerading to be) as opposed to making specific UI changes for each potentially slow element.

Regardless, I imagine the answer will be heavily dependent on what admins _actually do_, which is not something I'm overly familiar with.

title: Understand admin bandwidth concerns and optimise accordingly
body:
We have generally been of the impression that admins had great internet, and fast computers. This has led to a design where admins don't have a local DB, and everything is pulled over the network. This is potentially looking like it may not really pan out.

For example, in LG PROD (which is a small dataset in the grand scheme of things, they're just getting going) here is what my machine downloads when I refresh the page:

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/583851/14612566/a0416a78-058f-11e6-84ee-6ebba7b690c1.png)

Things you will notice:
- gzip is super important for us
- We download a huge amount of stuff, and there is a reasonable chance that we download the same thing multiple times

It ended up totalling ~12mb or so, which is either OK if you have great internet, or utterly terrible if you are on mobile internet.

This ticket is for us to answer these questions:
- What are the bandwidth expectations of admin users? Will they have unlimited bandwidth or should we be trying to target a rough amount used per day / month?
- What is the expected internet quality, re: fiber vs. broadband vs. 3g?

Which in turn helps us understand how much we care about this. Note: LG's dataset right now is presumably nowhere near as large as it will get when they start deploying to new locations, so these numbers will all go up quite a bit over time.

title: Run e2e tests in new db. Issue: #1825
CouchDB is not authorized to return `_all_docs` listed from POST but can return docs listed from GET
body:
The couch-to-postgres adapter uses `_all_docs` first to fetch all UUIDs in the system using `include_docs=false`.

Once all UUIDs are fetched, only the necessary UUIDs are requested from `_all_docs` by sending a POST with a list of UUIDs and using `include_docs=true`.

With the analytics user, I am able to GET `_all_docs` even with `include_docs=true`, but I cannot get a subset using POST `_all_docs` (regardless of `include_docs`). I guess POST might be used for other purposes so the entire verb is blocked from analytics?

Is there a way we can resolve this so the adapter does not need admin access? It might not be possible without fully rewriting the adapter to use a changes feed or something.

title: Establish a template for creating new databases
body:
Right now we have two schemas. three roles, and a set of default permissions for two of the users.

These can be created inside a template and then `CREATE DATABASE x WITH OWNER y TEMPLATE z` where z is the template containing all that nifty stuff.

This is all stuff that needs to be done by the postgresql superuser. So it can't be done by the adapter, it really needs to go at a level closer to #1801 

It might be nice if we can find a way to version control these settings so that they get deployed reliably.

title: Redesign Send Message (sending SMS)
body:
With 2.6 it has a few problems:
- With large datasets (ie LG) it downloads _insane_ amounts of data just to fill a dropdown.
- It's got a lot of dead code. Here is a [patch](https://gist.github.com/SCdF/b4ef336bc1535a756e0195346d8938cd) with a bunch of code deleted that it doesn't use (ie it's all noop for various reasons) (the `//!` comments is me working out how it can fit with [select2-ajax](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/develop/static/js/modules/select2-ajax.js))
- It uses the same amount of insane data to validate phone numbers afterwards
- It's not clear why it's invalidating the data, or if that can result in different contacts being affected
- **The concept of `everyoneAt` no longer works for 2.6**, because while in 0.4 all contacts were CHWs, in 2.6 many contacts are normal people, for whom you wouldn't want to mass spam (or would you?)

title: Non-XML form view support
body:
For 2.6 systems with XML forms, each form gets a table called `formview_{FORMNAME}_{FORMVERSION}`. Although they are tables, the `formview` predates working on 2.6.

For 0.4, each `formview_{FORMNAME}` is actually a view of the table containing all the JSON. As I work on an old 0.4 system, I realized this process of generating formviews automatically from JSON is not build into the adapter, but rather remains as a pl/pgsql function called `build_formviews()` in this file:
https://github.com/medic/middleware/blob/master/postgres/formviews.sql

For the old 0.4 systems, a bit of doing-this-by-hand is going to be required, and such support requests will be finite/limited. I'm not concerned about automating `build_formviews()` for them.

For 2.6 systems which might have forms that are _not_ XML, we should have some solution. If those forms end up looking like the 0.4 forms, then the above `build_formviews()` function should make its way into the adapter itself at some point.

If all forms, regardless of ODK and other considerations, end up being in XML for some reason, then no action is necessary.

title: Bootstrapping postgres tends to have different behavior than keeping postgres updated
body:
In practice, I found out that bootstrapping postgres from couch tend to operate differently than running the adapter on a populated database. So far, these differences have been acted on by the way in which the adapter is called: the adapter does not make any such distinction.

Technically, there doesn't have to be a difference, but practically there probably should be.

Let's use an example of a CouchDB database with between 50,000 and 300,000 docs (both are actual use cases I've dealt with already). Postgres is being freshly applied, so it has 0 docs in it.

node has limited system memory available. The following link talks about some of this, including the `--max-old-space-size` workaround I've had to use for dealing with audit logs. Any large docs, or any large enough set of small docs, can crash node with out of memory error.
https://bugs.chromium.org/p/v8/issues/detail?id=847

There is a balance between fetching enough data from couch in a single call to not run out of memory, but reduce the overall number of HTTP requests sent to the CouchDB server. We probably don't want a separate GET for each of 50,000 to 300,000 docs. There is a related balance in the interval between HTTP requests sent to CouchDB. If we did call a separate GET for each doc, we'd probably not want to do so in a very short interval of time.

Both the maximum number of docs fetched per interval and the interval itself are settings for the adapter. When actually running the adapter, we can get away with 100 docs every 15 minutes pretty safely (both staying on top of new data and not hitting out-of-memory when audit logs or very large docs come in). However, if we used that combination when there are 0 docs in postgres, we're talking about at least 5.2 solid days to get to 50,000 until we're "caught up" (which, by five days later, we probably aren't caught up).

So for bootstrapping, we might want to crank that up to 4000 docs every 3 minutes. We certainly don't expect that kind of throughput in normal use, so we wouldn't want that to be the normal settings after we've bootstrapped.

The problem is that when there are very large docs (audit_logs in 0.4 systems, possibly some kind of doc that might happen in 2.6 sometime in the future), we'll hit an out of memory and the adapter outright crashes when pulling 4000. So for some systems, babysitting the adapter is required while bootstrapping.

Perhaps there is some way to see how large the next batch of X docs is before downloading them, which can help generate a dynamic doc threshold when bootstrapping (or anytime really). Regardless, it might be worthwhile to consider the bootstrapping case and how we can incorporate it into the adapter (rather than babysitting or running with two different sets of settings).

title: Standardize table and column for the adapter
body:
When the adapter was first written, there were very few absolutes. It was meant to be very flexible.

The table and column are extra variables which allow someone to _potentially_ add a new column to an existing table.

So we have two variables which need special handling and a bunch of testing for various cases (is there a table? if there is a table, is there a column?).

The analytics stuff, in many cases, does not have access to those variables.So making them variable _really_ messes with analytics.

In practice we've been using the table `couchdb` and column `doc`.

If the table doesn't exist, then we should add it with the column. No other logic should be required for initialization of `lib/couch2pg`, so that excess can be removed from the code and the unit and integration testing. We can remove the table and column variables entirely and hard code couchdb and doc.

The reduced variables might also ease configuration stuff related to #1800

title: Move initial replication into bootstrap. Issue: #2394
body:
This moves the initial replication into the bootstrap layer which means it runs once per user+device+server, not every page load. The user will now see a spinner while the initial replication is going. This means they won't be querying the database until all the data is up to date which speeds up the overall initial replication time.

One downside is because this is running before Angular has started it's not easy to capture the replication data to show on the About page. I've tried to capture the same data and output it to the console. That combined with the fact the app won't load until the replication completes hopefully gives enough info about the state of replication. I'd welcome feedback here about how to include more information.

With this patch initial startup takes about 3.5 minutes with a real user on a tecno on a real server which includes downloading static resources, doing initial replication, getting the ddoc, starting angular, and waiting for the rules engine to start up. CPU usage is about 2-3% above baseline during the replication phase.

title: Restructure git branches
body:
### Master

Have a `master` branch as the default github branch. Commits are made directly into this branch or via PRs to this branch. Travis builds and publishes an alpha release every time a commit is made.
### Release branches

Have release branches which branch of `master` and are named `<major>.<minor>.x`, for example "2.6.x". This will gradually diverge from `master` so don't plan to merge this back in, but ensure all changes in the release branch are also in master (either by cherry-picking or merging in either direction). Travis builds and publishes a beta release every time a commit is made to a branch with this form.
### Final releases

Tag a release branch when it's ready for production named `<major>.<minor>.<servicepack>`, for example: "2.6.3". Travis builds and publishes a final release every time a tag is made in this form.

title: Increase stability by looping over changes

While it takes `curl` ~20 seconds to download an entire changes feed it can take node / the pouchdb library significantly longer, presumably because it's also parsing the JSON.

title: column "xyz" of relation "abc" does not exist when writing report data to database
body:
e.g.:

```
error: column "patient_dob" of relation "formview_assessment_2015-11-02" does not exist
    at Connection.parseE (/Users/scdf/Code/Medic/medic-analytics/node_modules/pg/lib/connection.js:539:11)
    at Connection.parseMessage (/Users/scdf/Code/Medic/medic-analytics/node_modules/pg/lib/connection.js:366:17)
    at Socket.<anonymous> (/Users/scdf/Code/Medic/medic-analytics/node_modules/pg/lib/connection.js:105:22)
    at emitOne (events.js:90:13)
    at Socket.emit (events.js:182:7)
    at readableAddChunk (_stream_readable.js:153:18)
    at Socket.Readable.push (_stream_readable.js:111:10)
    at TCP.onread (net.js:529:20)
```

This only occurs when you import a database in batches. This does _not_ mean it's not important: unless you delete everything and regenerate you're always importing in different batches over time.

What it _does_ suggest is that it's something to do with forms having different data in them even though the version is the same. This could be for two reasons:
- The data captured has changed but the version hasn't
- The way we're defining a field to be stored is not consistent across documents (for example, if a field is empty it's not presented to us)

Either way, if we're going to keep the xml extraction we need to deal with this somehow.

title: Design needed : admins sending reports for SMS + web instances
body:
Right now if you're a 0.4 instance, you're an SMS project, and admins send SMS reports with medic-reporter:
![screen shot 2016-07-04 at 16 08 58](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/911434/16563327/a70be816-4201-11e6-8dde-845895092eca.png)

And if you're a 2.x instance, you're on android, and admins send web reports from action button : 
![screen shot 2016-07-04 at 16 08 01](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/911434/16563307/891e1c70-4201-11e6-9877-65f3dd405a73.png)

When we merge SMS and android in 2.x, we'll have both types of reports enabled, so admins will have to pick between SMS and web form. 
It's possible that a system have only SMS, or only web (XML) forms, or both. 
If both, I don't know how the form names would be (the same or different?) Situations like this are already happening in 0.4 with textforms (JSON) + medic collect (XML), and I think the forms have different names, and separate configs. That might be something we want to do better at, but probably out of scope of this issue.

Anyway, design opinion would be great! Assigning @diannakane but feel free to reassign.

title: Always use the same pouchdb configuration
body:
The bootstrap code connects to the local db without passing any options. This means during initial replication auto_compaction is off and the db grows larger than needed until the app starts and compaction is turned on. Getting out of sync on other options would be much more significant (eg: `storage` which would replicate to one place, then try to connect to a different one).

A possible exception is the web worker adapter as we may not want to use it during initial replication.

Use the same configuration everywhere PouchDB instances are constructed. Find a way to ensure the configuration remains consistent, maybe a unit test, or publishing the configuration as a constant, or publishing to resultant PouchDB instance so we only ever make one for local and one for remote.

title: Legacy v0.4.x instances: remove socket limit in medic-api
body:
In https://github.com/medic/medic-api/blob/0.4.x/server.js#L31, we limit the maximum number of Express.js server sockets to 100. This proved unnecessarily low in the 2.8.x/master branch and was removed entirely, effectively making the limit infinite, which worked out okay. We never did the same for the older v0.4.x instances.

Symptom: nginx is timing out while attempting to connect to the local `medic-api` on port 5988. This repeats regularly for a while and then dies down:

```
2016/08/12 18:22:03 [error] 30226#0: *404098 upstream timed out
  (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream,
  client: 127.0.0.1, server: _, request: "GET /medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/add HTTP/1.1",
  upstream: "http://127.0.0.1:5988/medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/add", host: "localhost"
```

Theory: under heavy load, the pool of 100 sockets is exhausted and requests start getting dropped on the floor with no response.

Push an update to v0.4.x that removes `http.globalAgent.maxSockets = 100;` from the bundled Medic API, and does nothing else.

Seemingly unreasonable disk space requirements for 2.7.x to 2.8.0 upgrade
body:
Using a 45GiB production-like dataset, updating from `medic-webapp` version `2.7.2` to `2.8.0-b6` fills a 1 terabyte disk and eventually leads to `502 Bad Gateway` errors. CouchDB reports `{error,enospc}`.

Current understanding: when `medic-webapp` is updated via the Garden dashboard, the `medic` design document is modified. This potentially changes view code, which leads CouchDB to assume the worst and perform a full view regeneration procedure in the background. This procedure eventually fills the disk. One of the newly-generated `.view` files is approximately 40GiB; another is 10GiB.

Expected behavior: Naively, it seems like the space requirement for a full view regeneration should be no more than two times the size of the largest pre-rebuild view. At the very least, it seems like the required space should be no more than two times the total size of all pre-rebuild views (15GiB in this case). How we're regenerating more than 60GiB after a simple design document update is currently outside of my understanding.

To do: figure out why we're using so much space after an update to 2.8.0, then make it stop.

title: #2344 rhs actionbar
Allow for people-centric SMS workflows
body:
Existing projects with SMS workflows are case-based, exemplified by having a new ID for each new pregnancy for the same person. Actions in the app are now about contacts, as used by mobile app users, and we’ll want the SMS workflows to be person-centric as well. Having consistency between the two types of workflows will be easier for our team to design deployments and will improve how managers of SMS projects can interact with the webapp (eg view patient profiles, have tasks).

The goal of this issue is initially to raise any potential problems with this approach, then flesh out the features for implementation in the very short term (eg next 1-2 iterations), while highlighting those that can wait for a later milestone (eg in 2017).
## Proposal

To make this patient-centric we’d need to have the registration form create a person, and assign them a ID. This could be configured in app_settings like the other `Registrations`>`Events` (as of v2.9 this is `Report Actions` > `Events`). The newly created `person` contact would be within the same place as the CHW that sent the SMS, and viewing the patient’s profile in the webapp would show the unique ID. 

The CHW would use the 5 or 6 digit ID in subsequent messages about this person, similar to how the UUID is submitted with every form in the mobile app. They would not have an ID for each case eg pregnancy. 
## Acceptance Testing
- [x] A registration form can create a person within the reporting person's place, and generate a short `person_id` that corresponds 1-to-1 with the person UUIDs which can be sent with the auto-response.
- [x] The short `person_id` can be seen on the patient's profile.
- [x] Submitting a report with the short `person_id` would associate the report with the appropriate person. This means that when viewing the person's profile you would see all reports submitted about them under the history portion of their profile. 
- [x] From Registrations and Patient Reports we'd want to be able to access fields from the person's profile. _This is currently possible in case management eg `Thank you {{contact.name}}, visit for {{patient_name}} ({{patient_id}}) has been recorded.` With a patient-centric approach this would be something like `Thank you {{reporter.name}}, visit for {{subject.name}} ({{subject.patient_id}}) has been recorded.` I used `reporter` and `subject` here to avoid confusion between who is sending the report and who it is about, which may be the case if either contact or person is used. Open to other suggestions for labels._
- [x] A Patient Report form _clears_ all associated scheduled messages for a patient ID for the silence window (eg Delivery report prevents messages from going out for silence window)
- [x] An OFF Notification form _mutes_ all outstanding scheduled messages for a patient ID
- [x] An ON Notification form _unmutes_ all outstanding scheduled messages for a patient ID
## Features not implemented now
- Search for person's ID to avoid creating multiple profiles for the same person
- Update profile fields via SMS. For now this will be done by asking a manager to do it via the app.
- Manage families via SMS
- Updates to the ANC Dashboards to be patient-centric. This can be done at a later time using new widgets in Targets, which would be much more flexible and powerful.
## Background

Currently we use one and two step registrations for pregnancy or immunization reminders and follow up forms about a patient are submitted using the ID:

_One Step_

```
--> R Maxine 16
<-- Thank you, you have registered Maxine for pregnancy reminders. Her ID is 12345.
--> V 12345
<-- Visit for patient 12345 has been recorded.
```

_Two Step_

```
--> R Maxine
<-- You have registered patient Maxine. Their ID is 12345.
--> P 12345 16
<-- Thank you, you have registered patient 12345 for pregnancy reminders.
--> V 12345
<-- Visit for patient 12345 has been recorded.
```

Going over the workflows for existing priority use cases and we can complete them in similar or simpler ways using patient-centric approach. Below is a sequence diagram showing patient-centric interactions with both 1 and 2 step registrations as well as the continuity between use cases. PNC is not completely fleshed out as it is still being (re)designed (also subject to #2756).

![person-centric anc pnc immunization workflows 1](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/18605498/a6473c7e-7c61-11e6-8c17-5b70f3a3b92f.png)

_[**Edited** to transition from planning to feature request]_

title: Adding a space to a select2 search term creates a request that returns > 150MB
body:
To reproduce (make sure you have the network tab visible first):
1. Go to a CHP Area
2. Click Edit
3. Click on the supervisor dropdown to bring up the search box
4. Type in the name of a branch, then wait until you see the `contacts_by_type_freetext` view request.
5. Type in a space.
6. You should see a second `contacts_by_type_freetext` view request with no key. If you keep waiting (about 4 minutes in production), it will download what appears to be every contact (about 190 MB in production), and the window might freeze.

Can we add in some sort of protection so that adding a space to the end of a search term can't start a whole new search (`contacts_by_type_freetext` request)? This may not fit in with how other searches work, but this can cause some annoying performance issues, including the web app freezing and search results taking a long time to be returned.

title: If initial sync fails without syncing anything subsequent syncs get no results
body:
If you only have the ddoc in your local db then the changes request is [incorrectly determined to be a app status watcher](https://github.com/medic/medic-api/blob/2.8.x/handlers/changes.js#L326) instead of a data replicator meaning it only watches for ddoc changes. This affects 2.8.0 and master.

The workaround is to clear your IDB and try again, but with some users the initial sync is likely to fail again, leaving them unable to use the app.

title: Initial sync fails if server doesn't respond within 30 seconds
body:
With some users initial replication isn't responding quickly enough and the request times out. This means the app loads with lots of errors. Eventually the background replication should fix the app and a refresh will get back to normal but it's a jarring experience. It should have a heartbeat so timeout doesn't occur unless the server is unreachable.

Affects 2.8.0

Causes #2770

There have been a number of timeout errors which may have contributed Error: ETIMEDOUT at null._onTimeout (/var/adapter/{redacted}/medic-analytics/node_modules/pouchdb/node_modules/request/request.js:772:15) at Timer.listOnTimeout [as ontimeout](timers.js:110:15) And also a situation where the connection was terminated events.js:72 throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event ^ error: terminating connection due to administrator command at Connection.parseE (/var/adapter/{redacted}/medic-analytics/node_modules/pg/lib/connection.js:539:11) at Connection.parseMessage (/var/adapter/{redacted}/medic-analytics/node_modules/pg/lib/connection.js:366:17) at Socket. body:

It's not working very well on small screens:

body:
We create a document to store whether or not the first install stuff should run:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/583851/19768009/748de942-9c4d-11e6-97f3-e4bfb2f57d19.png)
Because we hide CouchDB behind medic-api, and medic-api has an endpoint called "login", this value can never be replicated externally (e.g. you use admin credentials to completely replicate a DB from one place to another). The replicator sees it needs to download a document called "login" and then gets confused when it gets HTML back from `https://blah/login`.

We should fix this by changing the name of this document to something else.
